claims: The Artemis II Orion capsule splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California, on April 10, 2026, at 8:07 p.m. EDT.
The splashdown occurred at 5:07 p.m. PDT.
The capsule landed roughly 40-70 miles off the coast of San Diego, California.
A recovery team aboard the USS John P. Murtha recovered the four-person crew.
The crew consisted of NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen.
The Artemis II mission marked the return of the first human flight to the Moon in over 50 years.
